6-dof-graspnet.value: Generating grasp poses for robot object manipulation by sampling grasps using a variational autoencoder from 3D point clouds.
Introduces a Grasp Sampler and Grasp Refinement networks that use a variational autoencoder and a grasp evaluator model to generate and refine grasps from depth-camera point clouds.
Demonstrates a model trained purely in simulation that achieves 88% success on diverse real‑world objects without additional real‑world training steps.
pickup 17 objects with a success rate of 88%
Use a variational autoencoder (VAE) to sample a diverse set of grasps in SE(3) from the latent space conditioned on the observed point cloud X.
Introduce a VAE-based generator that produces grasp proposals and an evaluation network (discriminator) that accepts or rejects them based on success likelihood, using the 3D point cloud X as input.
Generating diverse sets of stable 6-DoF robot gripper poses for single objects from a partial point cloud, covering all possible ways an object could be grasped.

A two-stage approach that learns a variational auto-encoder generator to sample grasp poses and an evaluation module that predicts grasp success and refines poses via gradient feedback, discarding low‑probability grasps to produce a final high‑quality set.
The grasp sampler is a deterministic function that predicts a grasp given a point cloud X and a latent variable z.
The latent space distribution is chosen as P(z) = N(0, I).
Different grasps are generated by sampling different z from P(z) for a given point cloud X.
The encoder Q(z | X, g) maps each pair of point cloud X and grasp g to a small subspace in the latent space z.
Optimize the loss function using stochastic gradient descent for each mini-batch.

During training, the decoder learns to decode a latent variable z sampled from N(0, I) to generate grasps, while the encoder learns to output z that contains enough information to reconstruct the grasp pose.
During inference, remove the encoder Q and sample latent values from N(0, I).
Implement both encoder and decoder based on the PointNet++ architecture, concatenating each point's 3D coordinate and feature vector with the latent variable.

Split the predicted grasp width ŵ_i ∈ [0, w_max] into 10 equidistant grasp width bins and represent ŵ_i by the center value of the bin(s) with the highest confidence.

Inject orthonormality of approach direction a ∈ R^3 and baseline direction b ∈ R^3 by coupling predictions through an in‑network Gram‑Schmidt orthonormalization, projecting and only predicting the component of a orthonormal to b.

Optimize a weighted, multi‑label binary cross entropy loss l_width for grasp width bin predictions, weighting bin losses anti‑proportional to bin size.
